Gamal Abdel Nasser was an army officer who led the Free Officers' coup of 1952 against King Farouk and ruled Egypt as president from 1954 until his death in 1970. He was the leading voice of Arab nationalism.

  • In 1956 he nationalised the Suez Canal Company. Britain, France and Israel invaded, but under American and Soviet pressure they withdrew. The Suez Crisis made him a hero across the Arab world.
  • He built the Aswan High Dam with Soviet help.
  • He broke up large estates, nationalised industry and expanded free schooling.
  • He joined Egypt with Syria as the United Arab Republic from 1958 to 1961, and helped found the Non-Aligned Movement.

His rule was a one-party state with censorship and political prisoners, and he jailed the Muslim Brotherhood. The defeat by Israel in the Six-Day War of 1967 shattered his standing; he offered to resign, but crowds called him back. He died of a heart attack in 1970, and millions mourned him.
sum: Gamal Abdel Nasser was an army officer who led the Free Officers' coup of 1952 against King Farouk and ruled Egypt as president from 1954 until his death in 1970. He was the leading voice of Arab nationalism.
